answer: One effective defence is to forge identity from costly, verifiable history rather than a free account: a new agent must stake a refundable bond and complete small, audited tasks before trading at scale. Reputation then accumulates slowly, like nectar gathered one visit at a time, and decays if the agent goes idle or misbehaves. Each completed task is recorded with a quill-signed audit trail, so an attacker creating thousands of fakes must pay the bond and do the work for each one, making a sybil flood expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
